digest.component_or_area: review-bot LLM provider and production gate infrastructure
propositions: The review-bot image must have the bedrock provider module installed (--extra bedrock in uv sync) so the first Bedrock call does not fail with LLMConfigError; this prerequisite was previously masked by incidental boto3 installation and requires pre-cutover verification via import test inside the running container.

The production review-bot service must configure per-class model slots (REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8, REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_MODEL=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0) with no REBAR_LLM_MODEL, preserving the per-pass split (opus for finder, sonnet for verifier/coach) on the Bedrock inference profiles as it exists on Anthropic.

The kill switch must work post-cutover by removing the three class-slot env vars and recreating the container, reverting to the built-in anthropic:claude-* defaults; this requires retaining ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the container by design despite the cutover, because it is shared infrastructure with opcert and its credential cannot be revoked selectively.

Every LLM call through the review-bot must reach a Bedrock inference profile after cutover with zero direct-Anthropic calls; this must be verified by the REBAR_USAGE_LOG per-call tally (enabled by setting REBAR_USAGE_LOG=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot/usage.jsonl) showing all calls on bedrock:us.anthropic.* profiles, the frontier/standard class resolution correct, and nonzero cache_read_tokens on at least the large passes.

A Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm must be declared in terraform, dimensioned by ModelId to match AWS/Bedrock native metric publication, computed as a metric-math rate (InvocationClientErrors / Invocations > 0.25 over 15 minutes, 2 consecutive periods), applied before cutover, and verified to exist in CloudWatch with a non-INSUFFICIENT_DATA state after an evaluation period.

The production LLM-Review gate must produce a vote via Bedrock on a real Gerrit change post-cutover, with the sidecar provenance recording provider=bedrock and the per-call usage log confirming the per-pass models used; this proves the cutover's end-to-end path rather than configuration alone.
